drafts.angle: Tracking 18 KPIs sounds thorough, but most outbound teams need a short list tied to pipeline stages — not a dashboard that reports activity while revenue stays flat.

linkedin.content:
Most outbound dashboards are full of numbers that don't answer the one question leadership actually asks: is this producing pipeline?

Expandi's guide on lead generation KPIs (link below) lays out 18 metrics across the full funnel. Worth a read — but the practical takeaway is simpler than the list: pick one or two metrics per stage, compare them against the right segment, and resist the urge to optimize for the numbers that are easiest to move. Open rates and connection accepts feel like progress. Meetings held and pipeline created are the ones that matter.

The danger isn't tracking too little. It's tracking activity volume and mistaking it for outbound health.

What metric do you actually use to decide whether an outbound sequence is working?

drafts.angle: The real story in 'AI GTM agency' growth isn't the AI — it's that RevOps-rooted operators already understood the levers; AI just removed the headcount bottleneck.

linkedin.content:
The 'AI GTM agency' story everyone's excited about is mostly a headcount story.

When a former VP RevOps strips out the coordination layer — researchers, ops coordinators, junior SDRs — and replaces it with well-scoped AI tooling, the margin math changes fast. That's the actual insight buried in a recent AMA recap from The GTM Engineering Newsletter (link: https://newsletter.gtmengineering.ai/p/ama-recap-how-to-start-a-1m-ai-gtm).

But here's what the framing misses: most GTM teams aren't starting from RevOps fluency. They're starting from a stack of disconnected tools and a mandate to do more with less. Before AI makes you leaner, you need clarity on what the motion actually is — ICP, sequencing logic, handoff points. The tooling amplifies the motion. It doesn't replace building one.

What's the part of your outbound motion you'd most want to remove human hours from right now?

drafts.angle: Real-time AI monitoring of live campaigns is a meaningful shift — but the approval layer humans still hold is where judgment actually matters.

linkedin.content:
Most outreach reviews happen after the damage is done — campaign stalled, reply rate dropped, no one noticed for a week.

Expandi's new MCP (covered on the Expandi Blog) connects an AI agent directly to live campaigns: it can flag slowdowns, compare sequence performance, and draft follow-up copy in real time. You still approve before anything sends. That last part matters more than the automation piece.

The real question isn't whether AI can monitor a campaign — it's whether your team has a clear standard for what 'good' looks like before it hands the wheel back to a human. Tooling surfaces the signal. Judgment decides what to do with it.

Expandi Blog: https://expandi.io/blog/expandi-mcp-for-outreach-campaigns/
